About

I am a Masters in Data Science student at the University of Washington, Seattle WA, and am currently working as a Graduate Research Assistant at the Paul Allen School of Computer Science advised by Prof. Zaid Harchaoui. My research focuses on style-aware text rewriting and controllable stylistic perturbation techniques for authorship obfuscation, and developing controllable Transformer-based systems via attribution-guided modeling spanning areas like constrained decoding and lightweight parameter-efficient model adaptation in LLMs. With 2+ years of experience as an Applied Scientist at JPMorgan Chase, I have expertise in designing scalable fraud detection, NLP, and Graph-ML systems with a strong focus on Semi-Supervised learning, Contrastive Learning, Computational Linguistics, and xAI. I have a proven track record in delivering production ML systems at scale, and have published work in ACL, IEEE and other venues, with research spanning controllable text generation, multimodal NLP, and fairness-aware AI.

Previously, at JPMC, I led efforts in conducting fundamental research on the theory and science of Gradient Boosting and Semi-Supervised Graph ML models in the Payments Fraud Prevention team to capture anomalies in transactional networks. My work spanned across building Computational Linguistics, Entity Resolution (Record Linkage) models for Sanctions Screening, and Ranking-based models (Learning-to-Rank) for resource-efficient KYC systems and scalable MLOps — using tools like Spark, MLflow, and AWS to productionize experimental models. I've also prototyped Fraud pipelines using Transformer-based Encoders & Decoders for Check OCR systems, and built internal benchmarks using Self-Supervised Contrastive Pre-Training.

I have also pursued research internships in Applied NLP at Samsung Research where I worked on building a scalable context-rich search system, and word-sense disambiguation models for Samsung Bixby Assistant, and Human-Centered AI at the Accessible Computing Lab (ACT), McGill University, where my efforts were aligned towards AAC-based research.

I am passionate about building ML systems that are rigorous, reproducible, and grounded in theory, while being engineered for deployment at scale. I'm particularly interested in working with professors focused on explainable ML, efficient GNNs, transformer-based models, or fairness and accountability in AI.

Let's connect if you're building something at the intersection of learning, reasoning, and responsible AI.

Research Interests

My core research interests lie at the intersection of Computational Linguistics, Natural Language Processing, Semantic Modeling, Human-Computer Interaction, Human-Centered AI, Causality, and Explainability. I focus on designing NLP systems that are interactive, explainable, and adaptable to diverse user needs, especially in contexts like Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC), Accessible Computing, and Assistive Language technologies. I'm currently seeking Research Assistantship opportunities where I hope to contribute to cutting-edge work in the areas of:

  • Sequence modeling for low-resource and interactive language generation
  • Human-Centered AI and HCI for high-stakes decision-making
  • Graph representation learning and Dynamic Networks
  • Contrastive and Self-Supervised learning for multimodal inputs
  • Probabilistic reasoning and causal inference
  • Human-in-the-loop NLP and user-adaptive systems

Projects

KeyCognition - Predicting Cognitive Load using Keystrokes
An AI system that predicts cognitive load purely from keystroke dynamics by using fine-grained keystroke features like dwell time, flight time, pauses, and error patterns in real-time.
Auto-Explainability and Evaluation of LLMs
Enabled interpretability and auto-evaluation of LLMs by developing a framework for Transformer Explainability that visualizes prediction attributions using Integrated Gradients
AI-Powered Child-Labor Prevention Platform
Grievance redressal platform that leverages multi-method statistical models to re-rank grievances for efficient prioritization using weighted-ranking
No-Code Algo-Trading Portfolio Manager
Platform to create/execute trades using a No-Code Drag-and-Drop UI. Powered by a Domain-specifc language framework that internally builds a trading algorithm powered by hybrid recommendation models to minimize the risk and shortfall for a specifc trade
Meta Kaggle Forum Posts Clustering
Clustering Meta Kaggle forum posts for insigts using Heirarchical Clustering + Fine-tuned Word2Vec to include Kaggle-specifc OOV words
